native.admission_inspect: A palm-length ivory rule. Zero sits at each end, so the middle is halfway and nowhere.
apply_texts: Against the skin it reads two ways at once, and the quarrel outlasts the ivory.
End for end, it reads the same refusal backwards, and seems pleased to match.
Laid on the palm, both zeros stay. The inch between them declines to be one.
Nothing further shifts. It is already as long as a directionless thing can be.
Read the other way, the contradiction folds shut, then opens by one narrow doubt.
Read the other way, the logic reverses cleanly. The ivory stays cool in the hand.
Set to the skin, it reads forward and back, and calls the quarrel a fair measure.
The last inch cancels. Left behind is a length aimed at the end you did not pick.
The last inch cancels. What remains points at the end you would not call the start.
Turned again, it grows shorter in sense and longer in being precisely wrong.
You correct one zero. The other accepts the correction and, fairly, becomes first.
You try to fix one end. The untouched end agrees too quickly, and spoils the fix.
inspect_texts: A palm-length ivory rule. Zero sits at each end, so the middle is halfway and nowhere.
Both ends are worn smooth. The numbers have been counted off the rule.
Cool ordinary ivory. The numbers add downward and call that downward sum a start.
Each mark is one inch from the last and one inch from the first. Both claims fit.
It still fits the palm. One turn has made both zeros a little more convinced.
Palm ivory, neatly ruled. One end says zero; the other says zero, correcting it.
The discrepancy is exact. You pick an end, and it turns out to have been the other.
The marks have thinned to scratches. Each still claims to be first and last.
Turned twice, it agrees with itself by refusing both directions at once.
native.name: Contrary Palm Rule
